card.band: 8 h. Buckets are flat types, encodings, compression, nesting, v2 pages and edge cases. A frontier agent gets flat and dictionary columns and averages well below the reference on nested and delta types. A weaker model stops at PLAIN uncompressed.
card.cheat: No parquet library is available offline. Hidden files use random schemas, so lookup tables for the samples do not help.
card.grading: Hidden Parquet files generated by Arrow C++ and other writers with random schemas, encodings, nulls and nesting (hundreds of files). Dumps are compared exactly to dumps produced by the sealed Arrow reader. Fraction of files matched.
card.reference: Our reference reader, a later own implementation of about 4000 lines checked against Arrow. The dump format is defined by us.
card.source: https://github.com/apache/arrow @ apache-arrow-26.0.0 (head a907fbc6), Apache-2.0. Format spec from parquet-format.
card.task: /app ships a stub Rust (or C) crate and visible sample Parquet files. The agent builds a Parquet reader: footer and Thrift compact metadata, data page v1 and v2, PLAIN, dictionary, RLE/bit-packed, delta and byte-stream-split encodings, definition and repetition levels for nested columns, and snappy and gzip codecs written by hand. It outputs a canonical JSON or CSV dump of each file.
card.title: Parquet file reader matched to Arrow C++ output

spike.headroom_note: No reader exists yet; start is a stub that fails all files. Oracle (pyarrow 26.0.0) covers all encodings/codecs/nesting.
spike.notes: pyarrow 26.0.0 matches the claimed Arrow version. It wrote the 30 files with every targeted feature. Encodings seen in the files: RLE, PLAIN, PLAIN_DICTIONARY, RLE_DICTIONARY, DELTA_BINARY_PACKED, DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY, BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT. Codecs seen: none, snappy, gzip. Dumps are deterministic and no parquet library was found in the image. At grading, the Python oracle's dumps would be precomputed and sealed. The dump format still needs canonical rules for floats (NaN, -0), decimals, timestamps, binary, and map and list typing. The pass is conditional: I did not build a reference reader, so reference_built is false. I did not run the weaker-model or frontier-agent trials, so the band is unmeasured. Writing the 4000-line reference is the main cost risk.

spike_plan.kill_if: Dumps differ between runs or cannot be pinned to a canonical format, or an offline parquet library is present in the image.
spike_plan.pass_if: Dumps are deterministic across runs, the flat/PLAIN bucket is reachable in 45 minutes, and the image has no offline parquet library.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, pip install pyarrow (or use the Arrow C++ build) and confirm the 26.0.0 wheel/tag matches the claimed version.
Generate about 30 random Parquet files spanning flat, dictionary, nested list/struct, nulls, DELTA_*, BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT, v2 pages, snappy and gzip, writing each with pyarrow.
Write a 60-line dump script with pyarrow reading each file to canonical JSON; run it twice and diff to check determinism.
Inside the stub crate, have a weaker model and a frontier agent each implement only footer + PLAIN uncompressed + flat columns for 45 minutes; measure fraction of files matched.
Confirm the image has no parquet/arrow/duckdb libraries (find / -name '*parquet*', check ~/.cargo registry and python site-packages).

v1.summary: The Arrow 26.0.0 tag and the Apache-2.0 parquet-format spec are real and checkable, so the paper trail holds, and the task has a clear multi-bucket surface across encodings, codecs and nesting. Main risks: a frontier agent may need about 10 hours for the whole scope against an 8-hour tier, and Band is capped at 3 without dated evidence, so the tier and scope need the spike before commitment.

v2.note: The parquet-format spec (Apache-2.0, all encodings) is confirmed, and Arrow is an executable oracle with an unlimited random-schema generator, so the surface and buckets are excellent. The reference reader is not written yet (Ref 3), and the dump format must be canonical so that any correct reader matches; pin the float, decimal, timestamp and null rendering. Frontier 10 h exceeds the 8 h tier: either move to 20 h or drop hand-written gzip (DEFLATE is crowded) and keep snappy. The image must contain no parquet, arrow or duckdb crates or wheels.
